items.stem: Which of the following is one of the recognition criteria for a provision under IAS 37?

options.text: A present obligation arising from a past event that is probable and can be reliably estimated
options.rationale: Correct: a provision requires a present obligation, probable outflow and a reliable estimate.

options.text: A possible obligation that might arise from a future event
options.rationale: That describes a contingent liability, which is disclosed, not provided for.

options.text: Any expense management expects to incur next year
options.rationale: Expected future expenses are not provisions without a present obligation.

options.text: A future operating loss the entity forecasts
options.rationale: Provisions are not recognised for future operating losses.

items.explanation: Correct: a provision requires a present obligation, probable outflow and a reliable estimate.

items.stem: Which TWO situations are accounted for by disclosure rather than recognition under IAS 37? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A contingent liability where an outflow is possible but not probable
options.rationale: Correct: possible-but-not-probable obligations are disclosed as contingent liabilities.

options.text: A contingent asset where an inflow is probable but not virtually certain
options.rationale: Correct: probable (not virtually certain) inflows are disclosed as contingent assets, not recognised.

options.text: A warranty obligation that is probable and reliably measurable
options.rationale: That meets the criteria for a provision and is recognised.

options.text: A decommissioning obligation that already exists and is estimable
options.rationale: That is recognised as a provision, not merely disclosed.

items.explanation: Correct: possible-but-not-probable obligations are disclosed as contingent liabilities.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: A company wants to recognise a provision for expected operating losses of a division next year. Why is this not permitted under IAS 37?

options.text: Future operating losses do not arise from a past obligating event, so there is no present obligation to provide for
options.rationale: Correct: there is no present obligation, so no provision is recognised.

options.text: Operating losses are always recognised as contingent assets
options.rationale: They are neither provisions nor contingent assets.

options.text: Provisions can only be made for tax
options.rationale: Provisions are not limited to tax.

options.text: The loss must instead be capitalised as an asset
options.rationale: An expected loss is not an asset.

items.explanation: Correct: there is no present obligation, so no provision is recognised.
